ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Korean AML/CFT framework: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 17299, 10 Feb 2021, as amended), Articles 5-2, 5-8 and 12; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Presidential Decree No. 31317, 14 Apr 2021); Criminal Proceeds Concealment Control Act (Act No. 16863, 31 Dec 2019); and FATF Recommendation 24 as implemented by KoFIU and the Financial Information Commission. Beneficial ownership data for a Yuhan Hoesa is maintained by financial institutions and made accessible to KoFIU, the National Tax Service, the Korea Customs Service, and the Supreme Prosecutors Office. No public UBO register exists.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, UBOs, directors, officers and commercial counterparties of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa must be screened before incorporation against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU/UK consolidated financial sanctions, the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs designation list, and KoFIU high-risk regime alerts. Enhanced due diligence is required for this medium-risk aviation spares distribution under the Specific Financial Information Act, including PEP identification for family members and close associates, source-of-funds verification, transaction monitoring with a 30-day refresh cycle, and adverse media checks. Screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IRO) of the Supreme Court of Korea (Commercial Registration System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Articles 19 and 289 of the Korean Commercial Act and Article 13 of the Commercial Registration Rules, every corporation must have a Korean name written in Hangul; a foreign name may be used only as a secondary transliterated mark. The four-tier naming doctrine is: (1) trade or object-identifying words; (2) business-scope or distinguishing words; (3) legal-form suffix, either Yuhan Hoesa or its Hangul equivalent; and (4) insertion of a corporate mark or emblem only if authorized. When a foreign name is transliterated, the phonetic Hangul form must not be confusingly similar to an already registered name. Latin, Chinese, and Japanese characters may appear in parentheses but shall not replace the Hangul name for registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant receives a written statement of grounds. Within 14 days of rejection, the proposer may file a written appeal with the senior registration officer of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction under the non-contentious registration procedure. The appeal must state the intended corporate name, the rejection grounds, and why the proposed name is distinguishable and lawful. If the second review refuses, a further appeal may be taken to the High Court as a non-contentious registration matter. During adjudication, the name reservation is extended pending the final administrative order, and legal counsels written opinion should be attached for novel trademark and civil liability issues.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Korean National Tax Service and banks will generally reject a pure virtual-office or mail-forwarding address for a Yuhan Hoesa engaged in wholesale of certified aircraft rotables and avionics surplus, because the business involves high-value cross-border invoices, VAT refunds, and customs declarations. Although the Commercial Registry may initially accept a shared office address for incorporation, NTS desk-review for corporate tax registration, bank KYC under the Financial Consumer Protection Act, and the Korea Customs Service importer-of-record rules require a physical office with lease contract, utility bills, business signage, and staff attendance. A virtual office is therefore permissible only temporarily and only if a registered agent maintains original books at a physical location and the real office is later normalized within 60 days.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: on-site verification of place of business by the district tax office and customs; inspection of lease, utility, payroll, inventory, import-export declarations, and VAT return supporting documents; unannounced visits when refunds exceed KRW 100 million or when the registered address belongs to a shared office. Quantified risk: around 35% for a medium-risk company using a virtual office in the first fiscal year; 10% for a fully equipped physical office with staff and inventory.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Sangbeop), Articles 172, 287, 289, 290, 292, 295, 317, 318, 331, 543, 560; Commercial Registration Act (Sangeop Deunggi Beob), Article 5.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local Registry Office of the Seoul Central District Court, under the supervision of the Korean Supreme Court Registration Division.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Jeonggwan) and Corporate Registration Application (Hoesa Seollip Deunggi Sinhcheongseo).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under Korean statutory law: a Yuhan Hoesa may be formed with zero share capital. However, if the shareholders resolve to adopt a stated capital, the full amount must be paid into a frozen escrow deposit account at a licensed Korean commercial bank before the registration filing; funds remain blocked until the certificate of incorporation is issued and cannot be withdrawn without board authorization after the statutory registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], A YUHAN HOESA UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA, HELD ON [DATE] AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE.

WHEREAS the Company has been duly organized by its founding shareholders, has adopted its Articles of Incorporation, and has satisfied all preliminary filing requirements; and

WHEREAS the Board of Directors has the duty to establish the corporate governance framework, approve the initial capital structure, designate banking authorities, fix the registered office, and appoint statutory officers;

NOW, THEREFORE, be it RESOLVED by the unanimous consent of the Board of Directors as follows:

1. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION AND CAPITALIZATION: The share capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation is hereby ratified. Every founder shareholder subscription is confirmed, and the aggregate paid-in capital amount shall be deposited into a specially opened restricted escrow account at a domestic Korean commercial bank. The Representative Director and the Chief Financial Officer are jointly authorized to maintain the account until the registry issue has been completed, after which the capital may be transferred to the Company's operational account only upon a separate board authorization.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Company shall establish and maintain corporate current accounts, foreign currency settlement accounts, and segregated escrow or trust accounts dedicated to aviation transaction proceeds. All payments, including SWIFT wire transfers and aviation escrow releases, shall require the joint signatures of the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer. For any payment amount in excess of KRW 100,000,000, the written approval of the Compliance Officer shall additionally be required.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The registered office of the Company is hereby fixed at [full address in Seoul, Republic of Korea]. This office shall serve as the statutory venue for service of process, production of books and records, and all official registry communications. Any subsequent relocation shall require a special resolution of shareholders and formal notification to the competent Registry Office.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: The following officers are duly appointed with immediate effect: (a) Choi Jung-ho, Chief Executive Officer and Representative Director; (b) Kim Seo-yeon, Chief Financial Officer; (c) Park Min-jun, Internal Auditor; and (d) Lee Ji-woo, Aviation Compliance Manager and Data Protection Officer. All officers shall hold office until the next Annual General Meeting or until their successors are lawfully appointed.

5. REGULATORY DELEGATION: The Representative Director is expressly authorized to execute, sign, and deliver all incorporation filings, bank opening documents, tax registrations, industrial licenses, aviation safety authorizations, and labor/employment registrations necessary to conduct the Company's licensed business. Each executed document shall be presented to the Board at the next meeting and ratified by written consent.

6. CORPORATE RECORDS AND STATUTORY BOOKS: The Company shall maintain the shareholders' ledger, board meeting minutes, tax invoices, tariffe voucher records, and asset disposal logs in accordance with Korean standards of corporate accounting and the Korea International Financial Reporting Standards. The books shall be kept at the registered office.

7. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board resolves that all lawful actions necessary to implement this resolution are ratified, and the Secretary is instructed to deliver certified true copies of this resolution to the Registry Office, banks, and regulatory agencies as required by applicable Korean law.

This resolution shall be effective immediately and is duly recorded in the minutes of this founding board meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation, Articles Drafting, and Attorney Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Supreme Court Registration Office (IRO Internet Registry) and Seoul Central District Court Local Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before incorporation, the entity must obtain a Preliminary Name Search Certificate from the IRO portal. The proposed Korean name must be exactly registered as [Company Name]+Yuhan Hoesa and must not conflict with existing trade names. In parallel, the founding attorneys must draft the Articles of Incorporation specifying the commercial purpose of wholesale distribution of surplus commercial aircraft parts, clause of capital, number of shares, board structure, and registered office in Seoul. The articles must be notarized by a Korean civil law notary. The corporation must ensure no prohibited business purpose is included that would require separate government pre-approval beyond the aviation parts distribution license. Filed online or in person with the Local Registry Office.
required_dossiers: Company name search certificate
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Notarization certificate of Articles
Founder shareholders' identification documents
Power of attorney appointing the formation counsel
Statement of registered office address and floor plan
Registered seal impression certificate (Inseung)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, select up to two substitute names and re-submit the name search portal application at no additional government fee. If the articles are substantively criticized by the registry examiner, correct the defective clauses within 14 days, execute amended articles, and file a supplementary notarized copy; the earlier filing date is preserved if the cure is completed timely.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription and Escrow Deposit at Authorized Korean Commercial Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Services Commission and licensed Korean commercial bank (acting as deposit and escrow agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the articles and name certificate are ready, the founders must open a temporary subscription account at a Korean commercial bank. Since the business scope will involve international aviation payments, the bank will classify the entity as Medium Risk, requiring enhanced due diligence. Each founder must remit the subscribed capital from their own domestic or foreign bank account and provide source of funds documentation. The bank will issue a Certificate of Capital Deposit stating that the full subscription funds are held in a restricted escrow account. No funds may be disbursed until the corporate registration certificate has been issued and the bank receives a certified true copy of the First Board Resolution authorizing transfer to the operating account.
required_dossiers: Preliminary name certificate
Subscriber identity and passport confirmation
Articles of Incorporation draft
Share subscription agreements
Bank account application declaring ultimate beneficial owners
Source of funds statements (tax records or aggregate wire records)
AML/CFT risk assessment questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further due diligence, submit a written explanatory memorandum, audited statements of shareholder income, or a regulatory reference letter. If the capital deposit certificate is delayed, apply to a second licensed bank and simultaneously renew the name certificate to avoid expiration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Incorporation Filing at the Local Registry Office and Issuance of Business Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Registry Office of the Seoul Central District Court, plus the National Tax Service (HomeTax) for automatic business registration notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the deposit certificate, the corporate registration application must be filed with the Local Registry Office in the district of the registered office. The filing must include the notarized articles, a form of company details, the certificate of deposited capital, the consent-to-acceptance forms of each director and auditor, and proof of the registered office. Upon approval, the registry will assign a corporate registration number and issue the corporation registration certificate. The National Tax Service receives the data electronically, and a local tax office issues the Business Registration Certificate (Sae-roejeong). This certificate activates the corporate income tax and VAT registration numbers.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Corporate registration application form (Form No. 5 of Commercial Registration Rules)
Certificate of deposited capital from the bank
Written acceptance forms of directors, auditors, and CEO
Registered seal impress certificate
Address proof of registered office such as lease agreement
Founders' identification copies
Power of attorney of formation counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a 'deficiency posting' or suspend order, complete the missing documentation within the resubmission period (usually 2 weeks), pay any supplementary fee, and present the corrected documents to the same examiner. If delay exceeds the legal window, withdraw the application, amend the articles if needed, and refile with a fresh application, allowing the prior deposit certificate if still valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Operational Banking Facility and Tax Invoice Electronic Interface Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (for AML governance) and National Tax Service (for electronic VAT issuance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company shall present the final corporate registration certificate, business license, and board resolution to its chosen commercial bank to upgrade the temporary escrow account into an unrestricted corporate operating account. The bank will create two segregated sub-accounts: one for domestic KRW operations and one for foreign exchange (USD) settlement. Simultaneously, the company must register for the National Tax Service's electronic tax invoice system (HomeTax) to issue e-invoices for all sales and purchases of surplus aircraft rotables. The compliance officer will establish an AML-appropriate approval matrix for SWIFT wire transfers, requiring dual signatures.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration
Business registration certificate from National Tax Service
Corporate seal and seal certificate
Board resolution authorizing the signatories and bank mandates
AML compliance manual (prepared in Korean and English)
ID copies of all board members and authorized signatories
Tax invoice registration application (Form 1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes additional AML restrictions due to the medium-risk aviation industry rating, accept a transaction monitoring arrangement under ESC, elect to limit the account to wire only, and obtain a pre-approved compliance charter. For tax invoice registration, file a mandatory correction via the HomeTax helpdesk; e-invoice issuance will be post-dated by no more than 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Aviation Spare Parts Distribution License, Fire Safety Permit, and Environmental Registration Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) Aviation Safety Policy Division; local Fire Safety Prevention Division; Ministry of Environment (MOE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the entity distributes surplus commercial aircraft parts (ISIC 4659), it is subject to the Aviation Industry Support Act and the Act on Safety Management of Civilian Air Craft. Application must be made to the relevant MOLIT regional office by submitting the corporate registration certificate, proof of a commercial warehouse or secured storage facility, and a compliance affidavit from a licensed quality assurance manager confirming that every part released for sale has an approved FAA/EASA/KCAC Form 8130-3 or equivalent authorized release certificate. Fire Safety Division must issue a license for storage of nonflammable metal aircraft components; no EIA full report is required if the warehouse floor area is under 15,000 square meters, but an environmental registration (Class E) must be submitted if hazardous coatings or liquid waste are handled. Civil Defense approval requires a fire extinguishing plan and structural load certification.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration and business license
Application for aircraft parts dealer distribution authorization (MOLIT Form)
Warehouse lease agreement and floor plan approval record
Quality assurance manual and traceability protocol for rotables
Fire safety facility completion certificate and civil defense inspection record
Environmental registration Form for low-impact storage (Class D/E)
Waste management manifest if battery or chemical-containing aircraft parts are handled
Proof of liability insurance coverage for aviation product distribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOLIT raises a quality/management deficiency, the company must appoint an additional aviation quality inspector and refile within 30 days. For fire safety, rectify the identified facility defects through a certified safety service provider and undergo a re-inspection. For environmental registration, file a supplementary clarification explaining that no outdoor storage of volatile chemicals occurs. If all administrative remedies are exhausted, an appeal may be lodged with the Korean Administrative Appeals Commission within 90 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) Aviation Safety Policy Office; Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) as industrial licensing coordinator; local Korea Fire Safety Institute and Ministry of Employment and Labor (MOEL) for workplace safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificate of Aircraft Parts Distribution and Surplus Rotable Sales (under Article 127 of the Aviation Safety Act and the Aviation Safety Management Regulations).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MOE), Korea Environmental Impact Assessment Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration (Class D/E) for non-production warehousing and distribution. Full Environmental Impact Assessment is not required because the activity is wholesale distribution without chemical or metal smelting. However, if the warehouse includes autoclave testing, battery storage, or chemical degreasing operations, the tier upgrades to a 'Confined Environmental Risk Assessment' (Class B).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from sanitary facilities and floor washing must comply with the Clean Water Act: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) ≤ 20 mg/L, Total Suspended Solids ≤ 20 mg/L, and pH 5.5-8.7 before discharge to sewer. Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) at the parts cleaning station shall not exceed 15 mg/m3 in the working area. Any obsolete aircraft batteries or hydraulic fluids must be collected by a licensed hazardous waste hauler and disposed of under the Waste Management Act, with manifest documentation retained for at least 3 years. General warehouse dust and airborne particulates are capped at 5 mg/m3 during transfer operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The facility must obtain a Fire Safety System Completion Certificate (Gyeongcheongso-bang) validated by the National Fire Agency, including a fire alarm system, portable extinguishers rated for at least 20 square meters per class, and an evacuation plan. A structural load inspection certificate for any rack storage over 5 meters must be submitted to the local government. Additionally, an Occupational Health and Safety Compliance Certificate from the Ministry of Employment and Labor is mandatory, confirming the assignment of a workplace safety manager, emergency drills, and fit-testing for personnel handling hazardous aircraft residuals.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, administered through the Home Tax Service (HTS) electronic portal at hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Korean Yuhan Hoesa or a foreign non-resident entity with a domestic supply obligation, the statutory tax identification (Business Registration Number / VAT ID) is obtained through Business Registration under the Value-Added Tax Act. A foreign non-resident without a domestic place of business must first appoint a domestic tax representative with a notarized power of attorney under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Submit the Business Registration Application through the Home Tax Service (HTS) or to the competent district tax office, together with the articles of incorporation, corporate registry certificate, foreign investment report where required, director/shareholder identification, proof of place of business, and tax representative appointment letter. For a domestic Korean LLC, business registration must also follow completion of incorporation at the Korean Commercial Registry; NTS then issues the 10-digit Business Registration Certificate which serves simultaneously as the Corporate Taxpayer Identification Number and VAT ID. Registration must be completed before or within 20 days after business commencement, and failure to register does not relieve VAT liability.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (resident domestic corporation; profits taxed at entity level under the Corporate Tax Act, with no pass-through for a Yuhan Hoesa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea has no check-the-box or comparable entity-classification election. The Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily a domestic corporation under the Commercial Act and Corporate Tax Act, and no statutory hybrid mismatch election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold; VAT registration is mandatory from commencement of taxable business in Korea. A simplified taxpayer threshold of KRW 80,000,000 annual gross revenue applies only to eligible small individual businesses, not to a corporate LLC distributing surplus commercial aircraft parts.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic Tax Invoices (e-Tax Invoices) are mandatory for all VAT-registered business persons under the Value-Added Tax Act. Each taxable supply must be issued through an e-Tax Invoice and transmitted to the Home Tax Service using an NTS-accepted channel: HTS web portal, integrated public or private e-invoice platforms, or API-linked accounting software. There is no per-supply pre-clearance or anti-fraud digital stamping regime; the NTS validates e-invoices in its central repository through real-time error checks after issue. E-invoice submission must occur within the statutory deadline prescribed by the Value-Added Tax Act, with severe additional taxes for late or omitted transmission.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The export of tangible goods, including certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus, is zero-rated under the Value-Added Tax Act only where the goods are declared to Korea Customs Service for export, physically leave Korea within the authorised export period, and the VAT-registered exporter retains full documentary proof of export and foreign-currency receipt. The recipient must be a non-resident buyer and title must pass to that buyer outside Korea. Domestic supplies within Korea, or goods diverted to the Korean market after leaving a bonded area, are not zero-rated. For qualifying offshore digital services, zero-rating applies only to B2B supplies to non-residents where place of supply and use are outside Korea; this payload is goods-based and therefore substantiated by customs export records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (Export Clearance / Export Bill of Entry)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the carrier evidencing actual physical export of the surplus commercial aircraft parts from Korea
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) / Korea Foreign Exchange Bank Export-Proceeds Settlement Receipt confirming receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the National Tax Service determines that an export zero-rating claim lacks physical export evidence, transport documentation, or timely foreign-exchange repatriation, the zero-rated treatment is retrospectively clawed back and the supply is reclassified as a domestic taxable supply at 10% VAT. Under the Framework Act on National Taxes, the NTS may impose additional taxes of up to 40% of the underpaid tax for fraudulent underreporting, 20% for negligent underreporting, plus daily interest, and the deficiency assessment period may be extended to 10 years for fraudulent conduct. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Customs Act separately impose penalties for non-repatriated export proceeds and false export declarations, including criminal referral and customs fines. Any input VAT credits previously recovered on zero-rated exports are redetermined and recoverable, and the taxpayer must retain the customs export declaration, transport documents, FIRC/bank settlement evidence, commercial invoice, packing list, and aviation technical documentation for the full statutory record-keeping period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (central bank) as statutory overseer of the foreign exchange market under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the Ministry of Economy and Finance retains regulatory policy authority for cross-border capital transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized current account and a registration-based capital account; the Korean won is widely convertible for genuine trade, service, and dividend flows through authorized foreign exchange banks, but it is not an absolutely unrestricted offshore currency. Current account items, including aviation parts import/export payments and after-tax profit remittances, can be cleared without prior central bank approval once the bank files the statutory foreign exchange transaction report. Capital account flows, including foreign equity injection and capital repatriation, are documented under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, or the prescribed foreign exchange information system notice, with timely reporting and purpose-code classification. Export receipts must be settled through an authorized FX bank within the statutory 18-month export collection window; there is no forced surrender to the government, and exporters may maintain the proceeds in foreign-currency accounts or convert them into KRW freely. Practical restrictions are documentary rather than administrative; an aviation spares trader must present invoices, shipping documents, end-user certificates, customs records, tax clearance, and transactional evidence to avoid mis-invoicing and sanction concerns. The Bank of Korea separately monitors excessive volatility and may smooth disorderly market conditions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its enforcement decrees, export proceeds must be collected and settled through an authorized foreign exchange bank in the name of the Korean exporter within 18 months from the date of export declaration; extension is available where justifiable grounds are accepted by the bank or regulator. There is no mandatory conversion ratio in the strict residency sense, because exporters are allowed to remain in foreign currency as a foreign-currency deposit or to convert to KRW at market rate; however, 100% of the export receipt must be routed to the authorized domestic banking channel and reported in the Foreign Exchange Information System.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Current Account (KRW and multi-currency clearing)
Capital Escrow Account for Foreign Investment Injection
Capital Escrow Account / Export Proceeds FX Deposit Account
Aviation Trade Settlement Escrow Account with sub-limit controls

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Very Low. For a Korean resident entity, a foreign fintech EMI is not a permitted statutory account-holding institution under the Banking Act, the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, or the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. It cannot issue KRW settlement accounts, cannot verify inbound foreign investment capital for the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and cannot meet the authorized foreign exchange bank prerequisite for export settlement. Consequently, the treasury plan must use domestic commercial banking rails; foreign EMIs may be used only for secondary non-statutory information messaging or third-party payout outsourcing if local banking law permits, but never as the primary clearing venue.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical appearance. Under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and the anti-money laundering enforcement decree, a statutory representative or an authorized corporate presenter must appear at the branch of the Korean bank for identification, biometric verification, and a compliance interview. Remote opening by a foreign director is possible only through the bank's global network video call process, but this is a market-practice exception, not a substitute for the in-person verification required for the official corporate account opening in the bank's Korean registry. A consular proxy opening with powers of attorney is not a standard path unless the bank's compliance committee pre-approves it.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete UBO identification when ownership is intermediated through two non-Korean shell holding companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of composite incorporation documents in Korea and each holding layer; ownership chart; shareholder register from registry to natural persons; powers of attorney; passports; initials-of-owner identification; source of wealth and source of funds declaration; bank statements for seed investment; audited financial statements; tax identification numbers; consent to UBO verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aviation surplus distribution raises dual-use/export controls and counterfeit unapproved parts concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FAA/EASA/CAAC cognizant authority approval chain and Form FAA 8130-3 or EASA Form 1; ITAR/EAR classification letter; UN Sanctions and Denied Persons screen report; customer end-user certificate; no-reexport undertaking; trading contract and aircraft part traceability document; quality assurance certificate; customs export permit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party escrow instructions create a payee/beneficiary mismatch and unexplained funds transfer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed escrow agreement; bank countersigned escrow instruction; sales contract; invoice; commercial invoice; packing list; bill of lading or airway bill; material inspection certificate; letter of indemnity; written instruction from both seller and buyer to bank; SWIFT statement of underlying transaction; prior bank transaction history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and absence of Korean economic substance constitute shell-company tax and AML vulnerability.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Korean office lease agreement; utility bills; payroll records for local employees; director's certificate of tax residency; notarized appointment documents with apostille; board resolutions authorizing bank signatories; CRS and FATCA self-certifications; Korean business license; employment and rent contracts; independent external audit report; evidence that aviation sales functions are actually managed in Korea.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use an authorized foreign exchange bank as the receiving statutory settlement bank. Funds must be remitted from the non-resident shareholder's own account in the shareholder's own name and credited to the Korean entity's capital escrow account. The SWIFT instruction must include the statutory foreign exchange purpose code for non-resident equity investment, the underlying subscription agreement reference, contract number, and the description Yuhan Hoesa inbound equity injection for aviation spares distribution. After receipt, the bank files the foreign exchange transaction report; the entity submits an FDI report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act if the shareholder is foreign and the investment will be finalized; then capital verification is performed via a certificate of inward foreign exchange remittance, bank statement, board resolution, equity subscription agreement, and audited balance sheet confirming the contribution is permanently available. No inbound funds may be split across EMIs.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For low-value rotable purchases and sales abroad, use SWIFT MT103 with full invoice and underlying contract reference; for high-value or contractually structured aviation parts transactions, use an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit confirmed by a top-tier bank, with sight drafts and documents against payment; for medium-risk established counterparties, use Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) with a collection bank instruction. All outbound payments must be made through an authorized FX bank, matched with the underlying export or import declaration to Korea Customs Service, assigned the appropriate trade-settlement purpose code, and supported by invoices, packing list, aircraft part certificates, and delivery evidence. Standby LCs may back the escrow or performance obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward exchange contracts (KRW/USD and other tradable pairs) on substantiated aviation import/export exposure, requiring underlying invoices and contracts.
Cross-currency swaps for matching long-term aircraft parts payables and receivables, limited to the amount and maturity of the underlying trade or capital liability.
Trade-linked FX options, collars, and barrier structures when the entity has a confirmed aviation spares purchase order or export order.

Non-deliverable forwards only in the exceptional case where the underlying future payment currency is not freely deliverable and the hedge is approved by the Korean bank's market-risk control and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act review; speculative open NDF positions are not compliant.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and payment of final corporate income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Home Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, by 31 March; if the return is prepared by a certified tax accountant and filed electronically, by 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing surcharge of 20% of unpaid tax, under-reporting surcharge of 10% (40% for fraudulent under-reporting), daily late-payment interest at the statutory NTS overdue rate, enforced tax seizure, and eventual deregistration or strike-off of the business registration for persistent delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax (resident surtax on corporate income) annual return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (si/gun/gu) at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same filing window as the corporate income tax return: within 3 months after fiscal year-end; 31 March for calendar-year companies, or 30 April if tax-accountant e-filed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of up to 20% of the local tax amount, daily late-payment interest, coercive collection, and attachment of corporate assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular members' meeting approval of annual financial statements, surplus appropriation, and appointment of auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Members' general meeting; minutes and resolutions maintained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, no later than 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government penalty, but failure to hold the meeting invalidates annual accounts, exposes managing members to fiduciary liability, and in an audited entity may constitute a statutory audit violation attracting administrative fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax final returns for the two statutory supply periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Home Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First VAT period (January-June): final return by 25 July; second VAT period (July-December): final return by 25 January of the following year; preliminary quarterly prepayments due 25 April and 25 October.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 20% of the unpaid VAT amount, daily late-payment interest, enforced collection, and cancellation of VAT registration for habitual delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested enterprise annual status report (applicable if foreign shareholders registered under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE); submitted through the designated foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year, or by 31 March for calendar-year companies; any change in registered foreign investment matters must be filed within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 2 million, loss of foreign-investor registration protection, revocation of tax incentives, and corrective orders from MOTIE.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer year-end payroll withholding reconciliation report and annual withholding statements to employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS); employee copies retained as statutory records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Reconciliation return due no later than 10 March following the tax year; annual withholding statements must be provided to employees by the end of February.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Withholding negligence surcharge of 10-20% on unreported or under-withheld amounts, daily late-payment interest, and administrative penalty for failure to issue employee statements.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent certified CPA audit is compulsory under the Korean Act on External Audit of Corporations if the Yuhan Hoesa meets any of the following at fiscal year-end: total assets of at least KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 8.9 million); total liabilities of at least KRW 7 billion (approximately USD 5.2 million); annual gross revenue of at least KRW 20 billion (approximately USD 14.8 million); or an average of 300 or more full-time employees. Regulatory designation, securities issuer status, court order, or creditor request may also trigger mandatory audit regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) applies to companies subject to external audit and to consolidated financial statements; non-audited small and medium Yuhan Hoesa entities may prepare under Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP / Korean Accounting Standards).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Korean commercial law, an unlisted Yuhan Hoesa has no separate annual UBO confirmation return. Ownership is recorded in the Register of Members and updated contemporaneously. A share or membership transfer requires company approval and register endorsement; if a foreign investor is involved, the transfer or change in foreign equity holding must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act within 30 days. For AML/KYC purposes, financial institutions require beneficial-owner identification to be confirmed at account opening and periodically refreshed, and managing members must keep current UBO information available to the registered agent and statutory auditor.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 7,000 - 25,000 (full audit if statutory thresholds are met; review or compilation engagements range from 3,000 to 8,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The 21% national headline corporate income tax rate applies to taxable income above KRW 20 billion. A 10% local income tax surcharge is added, producing a combined top effective rate of 23.1%. No patent box or special aviation-sector holiday applies to this surplus aircraft parts distribution company. General Korean incentives include R&D tax credits (up to 25% of qualifying R&D expenditure), job-creation tax credits, temporary investment tax credits, and, for qualifying foreign-invested businesses operating in Korean Free Economic Zones, reduced or exempt corporate tax for up to 5 years. This company, unless separately approved, is taxed at the ordinary corporate income tax rates under the Corporate Income Tax Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Amount Return (Form 110) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal (www.hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; interim semi-annual preliminary corporate income tax payments are also required every fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and tax payment must be filed and paid within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, the statutory deadline is 31 March of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all domestic and export revenue from the distribution of certified civil aircraft rotables, avionics surplus, and related logistic services. Where the Korean company receives invoice-issuing fees or commissions from offshore affiliates, include those amounts as revenue. If title, risk, and control remain in Korea, the full sales amount is Korean source revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing inventory and cost of sales
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the cost of surplus aircraft parts, certification and overhaul costs, freight, insurance, customs duties, and warehousing expenses. Related-party purchase prices must comply with the arm's length principle; an overstated transfer price will require a taxable income upward adjustment by the Korean tax authority.

Gross profit equals Box 1 less Box 2. For a cross-border aviation parts trader, the gross margin must be economically supported by distribution functions, inventory risk, and certification control exercised in Korea. Unexplained thin margins in the presence of high sales volume are a classic transfer pricing red flag.

Include Korean payroll, rent, professional fees, insurance, bank charges, certification testing expenses, and ordinary trade-related entertainment within statutory ceilings. Payments to foreign affiliates for management fees, IT services, or support services are deductible only if there is a written contract, actual service evidence, and proportionality. Any foreign service fee paid to a non-resident without withholding tax is subject to reclassification and penalty.

Operating income is the result after deducting Box 4 from Box 3. If the Korean entity reports a persistent operating loss while the group is globally profitable, the Korean National Tax Service may apply the resale price method or TNMM to impute arm's length operating income to the Korean distribution entity.

Include interest income, dividends, foreign exchange gains or losses, rental income, and other non-operating items. Interest-free or low-interest loans from or to foreign shareholders are subject to deemed interest and thin capitalization restrictions. Interest owed to a non-resident is subject to 22% statutory withholding tax unless a bilateral tax treaty reduces it.

Pretax accounting net income under Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) or Korean GAAP. For a non-resident-owned Korean company, pretax income should reconcile with actual bank flows and inventory movements; unexplained paper losses can trigger a tax audit and personal tax negligence penalties for directors.

Schedule adding back non-deductible expenses such as fines, penalties, political contributions, excessive entertainment, and non-deductible taxes; and deducting non-taxable income, tax-exempt dividends, and reserves approved by tax law. Cross-border expenses not substantiated with proper documentation must be added back here.

Deduct unused tax losses carried forward within the statutory 5-year limit. The Korean entity cannot deduct losses incurred by its foreign parent or by a foreign subsidiary. A substantial ownership change may restrict the carryforward deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income and progressive corporate tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the Korean progressive brackets: 9% for taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 19% for the slice over KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion, and 21% for the slice exceeding KRW 20 billion. Compute the 10% local income tax surcharge separately. The Korean company, not its foreign shareholders, is the taxpayer for this tax.

Claim foreign tax credits for foreign-source income included in the Korean tax base, dividend tax credits, and credit for semi-annual preliminary corporate tax payments already paid. The foreign shareholder's dividend withholding tax is not deducted here; it is withheld at the time of profit distribution.

Enter the final balance payable to the National Tax Service. Any unpaid amount draws daily late-payment interest and may lead to collection seizure. The representative director must ensure settlement from the Korean corporate bank account; using an offshore account to pay Korean taxes is a serious violation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an additional tax equal to 20% of the underpaid tax under Article 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes; fraudulent non-filing or aggravated concealment triggers 40%. Unpaid taxes accrue statutory daily late-payment interest under the National Tax Collection Act. Criminal liability may arise under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, with imprisonment and fines for fraudulent evasion; if the evaded tax exceeds KRW 500 million, aggravated imprisonment can apply.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22.0% (20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply the reduced withholding tax rate under a bilateral tax treaty, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction, complete the Korean National Tax Service non-resident tax treaty application form, and prove actual beneficial ownership of the dividend, interest, or royalty. Documentation must be submitted to the Korean withholding agent before payment. If the full statutory rate has been withheld, a refund can be claimed by filing an application for refund with the District Tax Office within the statutory claim period, attaching the TRC, dividend resolution, shareholding certificate, invoice/loan agreement or IP license, and a statement that the recipient is not an intermediary, nominee, or conduit entity.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on outbound royalties and interest is 20% national tax plus 2% local surcharge, totaling 22%. Under most Korean double tax treaties, interest and royalties are reduced to 10%, and dividends to 15% generally or 5% for substantial corporate shareholding of at least 10% to 25% of the voting shares, depending on the specific treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5,000,000,000 for the Local File and KRW 10,000,000,000 for the Master File; documentation must generally be submitted with the corporate tax return or within a request period set by the National Tax Service
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not maintain a named Economic Substance Regulations regime identical to the UAE, but the National Tax Service and Korean courts apply the general anti-abuse substance-over-form doctrine. For an aircraft parts distribution company, the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) are procurement decisions, inventory risk, aircraft parts certification and airworthiness coordination, freight logistics, order processing, credit control, and contract execution. These functions must be performed in Korea by real employees, with actual board decisions and substantive contracts. A paper entity lacking personnel, premises, inventory, bank account, and risk exposure will be recharacterized, denied treaty benefits, and subjected to penalties and criminal tax investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Yuhan Hoesa exists only as a registered mailbox entity, has no real office or operational staff, keeps no inventory, exercises no procurement or certification control, and merely passes dividends and profits to an offshore affiliate in a low-tax jurisdiction while claiming treaty relief on Korean-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, transactions may be recharacterized according to economic substance. Unsettled tax liabilities attract an additional tax of 20% or 40% under Articles 47-2 and 47-3. Criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act can result in imprisonment up to 2 years or fines equal to multiple amounts of evaded tax; aggravated penalties apply for evasion exceeding KRW 500 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts pierce the corporate veil when a company is used as a fraudulent device. Directors can be personally liable under Article 401 of the Korean Commercial Act for damages caused to third parties and the tax authority. The representative director may be blacklisted as a delinquent taxpayer, restrained from overseas departure, face seizure of personal assets, and be sentenced to imprisonment for participating in tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Falsified Intercompany Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean distributor sells surplus aircraft parts to a related Singapore or Hong Kong trading company at a deliberately depressed price, while the offshore affiliate resells the parts at a substantial profit. No Local File or Master File is prepared, no comparable analysis exists, and invoice terms are inconsistent with the actual functions, risks, and assets attributable to the Korean company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service will readjust taxable income to the arm's length price under the Corporate Income Tax Act transfer pricing provisions. The under-reported tax is increased by the unfaithful return penalty of 40% if egregious, plus daily late-payment interest. Failure to submit required transfer pricing documentation is separately penalized and may support criminal tax fraud charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly executes false invoices or dominates the Korean entity to channel profits abroad cannot hide behind limited liability. The commercial court will impose civil liability for lost tax revenue, the personal bank accounts of directors can be frozen, the director may be placed on the National Tax Service blacklist with travel restrictions, and the Tax Investigation Division may recommend imprisonment for aggravated tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Remit Non-Resident Dividend, Interest, and Royalty Taxes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean company pays dividends to foreign shareholders and pays overseas management royalties, license fees, or shareholder loan interest without withholding the statutory 22% and without obtaining any tax residency certificate or treaty exemption file. The payments are booked as deductible expenses without third-party evidence or withholding tax declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent is liable for the uncollected tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Additional penalties of 20% or more, late-payment surcharges, and criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act may be imposed. The foreign recipient loses the ability to claim treaty relief because the withholding obligation was not fulfilled in a timely procedural manner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director who ordered the unauthorized foreign payments is jointly and severally liable for the withheld taxes, penalties, and interest. Such conduct is treated as a breach of the director's fiduciary duty under the Korean Commercial Act, can lead to personal asset seizure, a departure ban, inclusion in the tax delinquent blacklist, and criminal imprisonment for intentional failure to comply with Korean withholding law.
